- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 20–40% if preceded by a spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 10–30% for 3–5 day lagged declines.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment spikes from 0.00 to 1.00 — leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor of 0.7–0.8 to forecast peaks.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is > 2.0 above recent 18-day average, reduce by 15–25% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 1.00 → 0.00 → 1.00), model often misjudges turning points; use sentiment momentum (last 3 sentiment values) to adjust horizon-specific bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 0.5, model often fails to recognize low volatility; apply floor correction to prevent negative forecasts unless sentiment is clearly bearish.
